_comment: MarketPulse geopolitical risk overlay — HAND-MAINTAINED, not a live feed. Edit this file and refresh the Macro page to update markers/shading/ticker. Statuses: Normal | Elevated | Disrupted (chokepoints), risk: low | medium | high (conflict/sanctions). Coordinates are [lat, lng]. Flow figures are approximate shares of GLOBAL seaborne oil/trade and should be reviewed against current sources (EIA, UNCTAD).

chokepoints.name: Strait of Hormuz
chokepoints.flowLabel: ~20% of global oil & most Gulf LNG — near-shut since mid-2026
chokepoints.note: The world's most critical oil chokepoint is effectively closed following the 2026 US-Iran war: transits have collapsed to a fraction of the ~85/day baseline amid repeated attacks on shipping, the seizure of the tanker Amara and a fatal strike on the Minoan Dignity after Iran's ceasefire lapsed. Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline — the main overland bypass — was struck on 11 Sep and remains offline, leaving no fully open alternate corridor.
chokepoints.marketImpact: India imports ~85% of its crude, a large share via Hormuz. With the strait now effectively shut, the tail risk has become the base case: Brent spike → OMC marketing-margin squeeze (watch IOC, BPCL, HPCL), fatter import bill → INR depreciation, wider current-account deficit and stickier CPI → pressure on RBI to hold/hike. Upstream names (ONGC, OIL) act as a partial hedge; paints, tyres, aviation (crude-linked input cost) are negatively geared.

chokepoints.name: Strait of Malacca
chokepoints.flowLabel: ~25% of world seaborne trade, ~16 Mbbl/d oil
chokepoints.note: Primary artery linking the Indian Ocean to the Pacific — most Gulf crude bound for China, Japan and Korea passes here, as does a large slice of India's east-bound trade. Open and operating normally (the littoral states — Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore — have reaffirmed free passage), but now under heightened scrutiny as the main chokepoint absorbing traffic rerouted away from a shut Hormuz.
chokepoints.marketImpact: A blockage reroutes shipping around Indonesia (Lombok/Sunda), lifting freight and insurance costs → costlier imports and squeezed margins for Indian exporters and importers alike. Broadly risk-off for trade-geared sectors; container/logistics rates spike.

chokepoints.name: Bab-el-Mandeb
chokepoints.flowLabel: ~10-12% of seaborne oil; gateway to Suez
chokepoints.note: Southern gate of the Red Sea / Suez corridor. A Sep 2026 Houthi offensive down Yemen's Red Sea coast captured the port of Mokha and Perim Island inside the strait itself, handing a non-state group territorial leverage over the chokepoint. Maersk and Hapag-Lloyd have paused transits, pushing carriers onto the Cape of Good Hope detour (+10-14 days).
chokepoints.marketImpact: Directly hits India-Europe trade lanes: longer transit and elevated freight/insurance raise costs for exporters of textiles, chemicals, engineering goods and pharma to Europe, and delay inbound cargo. Container freight indices spike; shipping/logistics names see volatile pricing.

chokepoints.name: Suez Canal
chokepoints.flowLabel: ~12% of global trade, ~9% of seaborne oil
chokepoints.note: The Europe-Asia shortcut. Effective throughput is deeply cut as the Bab-el-Mandeb gateway downstream deteriorates — with major carriers pausing Red Sea transits in Sep 2026, much Europe-Asia cargo is again routing around the Cape.
chokepoints.marketImpact: Reduced Suez transit lengthens Europe-Asia voyages and raises freight for Indian export sectors selling into Europe. Knock-on to global supply chains and input costs; watch export-heavy engineering, textiles and specialty chemicals.

chokepoints.name: Panama Canal
chokepoints.note: Key Atlantic-Pacific link for US grain, LPG/LNG and container flows; throughput is drought-sensitive due to freshwater lock operation. A renewed El Niño drought has forced fresh capacity cuts — daily transits stepped down from 36 to 34 (3 Sep) to 32 (15 Sep) with tighter draft limits, as watershed inflows ran ~44% below average.
chokepoints.marketImpact: Limited DIRECT India exposure. Matters indirectly via US-Asia LPG/LNG and container rates — sustained restrictions can nudge global gas and freight prices, a second-order input for Indian importers.

conflicts.name: Russia-Ukraine War
conflicts.note: Now a battlefield stalemate with long-range strikes on both capitals, running alongside the most serious peace push in years — US envoys (Witkoff, Kushner) shuttling between Moscow and Kyiv and short truces attempted, though no durable ceasefire has held. Still disrupts Black Sea grain/fertiliser and European energy flows.
conflicts.marketImpact: Sunflower oil, fertiliser and wheat supply shocks feed India's food-inflation and input costs (fertiliser subsidy, agri-input names). Energy-price volatility supports discounted-Russian-crude flows to Indian refiners.

conflicts.name: Israel-Gaza / Levant
conflicts.note: A fragile de jure Gaza ceasefire has held on paper since Oct 2025 but a de facto low-intensity war continues, set against the far larger 2026 US-Iran war that has already spilled into Gulf shipping and oil infrastructure.
conflicts.marketImpact: The escalation-toward-Hormuz tail risk has now materialised (see Strait of Hormuz) — the crude-price channel is the dominant transmission to Indian markets. Gold catches a strong safe-haven bid.

conflicts.name: Israel-Hezbollah / Lebanon
conflicts.note: War between Israel and Hezbollah since Mar 2026 (opened after the US-Iran war and the killing of Hezbollah's leader); a de jure ceasefire since 16 Apr 2026 remains fragile, with Israeli operations continuing into September. 4,000+ killed and over 1 million displaced.
conflicts.marketImpact: Primarily a regional-escalation and crude-risk channel for India rather than a direct trade link — a wider Israel-Iran-Hezbollah flare-up reinforces the Gulf oil-supply premium (see Strait of Hormuz) and supports gold.

conflicts.name: Yemen / Red Sea
conflicts.note: A Sep 2026 Houthi ground offensive down Yemen's Red Sea coast took Mokha and Perim Island, escalating the Bab-el-Mandeb disruption from missile/drone attacks to territorial control of the strait.
conflicts.marketImpact: See Bab-el-Mandeb — elevated freight/insurance on India-Europe lanes.

conflicts.name: Sudan Civil War
conflicts.note: Civil war with humanitarian and regional-stability spillover; gum arabic supply risk.
conflicts.marketImpact: Sudan supplies a majority of world gum arabic (a food/beverage stabiliser input); disruption is a niche input-cost risk for FMCG. Limited direct Indian market impact otherwise.

conflicts.name: Sahel Instability
conflicts.note: Coups and insurgency across Mali/Niger/Burkina Faso; uranium and gold supply relevance.
conflicts.marketImpact: Niger is a notable uranium supplier; regional gold output is meaningful. Mostly a global-commodity tail risk, minor direct Indian exposure.

sanctions.name: Russia
sanctions.note: Energy, finance and tech sanctions. Indirectly benefits Indian refiners via discounted crude; complicates payments/insurance.

sanctions.name: Iran
sanctions.note: Oil-export sanctions tightened further after the 2026 US-Iran war; with Hormuz effectively shut, Iran is the central swing factor for Gulf tension and crude prices flowing through to India.

sanctions.name: North Korea
sanctions.note: Broad UN sanctions; negligible direct Indian trade exposure.

sanctions.name: Venezuela
sanctions.note: Heavy-crude export sanctions; marginal effect on global heavy-crude availability for complex refiners.

sanctions.name: Syria
sanctions.note: Broad sanctions; negligible direct Indian market impact.

sanctions.name: Myanmar
sanctions.note: Targeted sanctions post-coup; some India border-trade and gas-import relevance.

sanctions.name: Belarus
sanctions.note: Potash-export sanctions tighten global fertiliser supply — an input-cost channel for Indian agri.

sanctions.name: Cuba
sanctions.note: Long-standing US embargo; negligible Indian exposure.
